Consult Summary:
- Suspected urinary tract infection presenting with lower abdominal pain and mild systemic symptoms; plan for a 3-day antibiotic course to be started via pharmacy.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Two days of lower abdominal pain with feeling hot and sweaty; mild nausea; no vomiting.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began two days ago; no prior similar episodes.
- Location: Pain in lower abdomen, midline.
- Associated symptoms: Slight pink-tinged urine; increased urinary frequency; increased thirst; no dysuria reported; no vomiting; no acid reflux.
- Bowel habits: Had constipation last week, now normal; last bowel movement two hours ago and normal.
- Urine/stool: Light pink urine; no blood in stool reported beyond urine.
- Other symptoms: No back pain; no discharge.
- Past medical history: None significant.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Medications: None regular; no OTC meds.
- Contraception: Internal contraceptive implant for about one year.
- Social history: Lives with parents; drinks alcohol (about four beers per week); does not smoke.
- Family history: Mother with breast cancer.
- Exam/investigation notes: Temperature measured by patient around 37°C (afebrile); no other vitals provided.

Examination:
- Vital signs: Temperature ~37°C.
- Examination findings: Not documented.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Possible lower urinary tract infection (UTI).

Plan:
- Antibiotic therapy: Three-day course for presumed UTI; start via Babylon pharmacy; take twice daily for 3 days. Specific antibiotic name, dose, and route not documented.
- Safety/monitoring: If pain worsens, high fever, back pain, or new symptoms or lack of improvement, contact/return for possible face-to-face assessment.
- Follow-up: If symptoms persist or recur after treatment, further evaluation as advised.
- Additional notes: No imaging or lab tests ordered at this time.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Full vital signs beyond temperature (BP, HR, RR, O2 saturation) not provided.
  - Urinalysis or urine culture results not documented.
  - Pregnancy status or testing not discussed.
  - Complete medication reconciliation (drug name, dose, route, frequency) for the planned antibiotic not documented.
  - Immunization status and comprehensive physical exam findings not provided.
- Internal conflicts: None detected.
- Transcript quality: Some incomplete or fragmented phrasing and repetition; overall understandable. No explicit misstatements identified.
